If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The problem originates in the way the DefaultParser processes the default options passed as a Properties instance to its parse method. The parse method calls handleProperties after processing the command line arguments. In handleProperties, each property key (option) is checked; if the CommandLine does not already contain the option, it is added via handleOption.

Looking closely at handleOption, it calls updateRequiredOptions to update the expected required options and to set the selected option in an OptionGroup, if applicable. But this updating only occurs for options passed directly as command line arguments before handleProperties is called.

The root issue is that when adding options from the default properties, handleProperties does not check whether adding these options violates any constraints of option groups, namely mutual exclusivity. For example, if 'a' is selected from the command line and 'b' is set in the properties as default (and they are in the same OptionGroup), the group state is not checked or updated for 'b' added via default properties. This allows mutually exclusive options from the properties to be added alongside options from the command line without conflict detection. Hence, the OptionGroup's selected option is not correctly managed for defaults, causing the parser to not complain and the CommandLine to end up containing both 'a' and 'b'.

Although updateRequiredOptions sets the selected option in the group, this method is called via handleOption in handleProperties, so superficially it seems like the group should be updated. However, the key missing behavior is a check for conflicts in option groups preceding the selection/update. handleProperties adds default options without verifying if another option in the same group was already selected, contrary to the behavior for options from the command line.

This matches the bug report that "The state of the option groups is neither checked nor updated when the default options ... are processed," resulting in a CommandLine containing mutually exclusive options without error.

Recent bug reports about default options not being taken into account for required options further support the notion that default options handling in this parser is incomplete and inconsistent, though they focus more on required options rather than option groups.

In summary, the DefaultParser fails to enforce the mutual exclusivity constraint for options set via default properties, allowing multiple option group members to be selected when they should be mutually exclusive.

The key location responsible for this is the method handleProperties, which adds options from default properties without proper option group conflict checks. The method updateRequiredOptions does perform some updates but does not prevent violations or throw exceptions if a conflicting group option was already selected. This causes the observed erroneous state.

---

Next steps would be to check that handleProperties and possibly updateRequiredOptions enforce these mutual exclusivity constraints for options coming from the Properties used as defaults.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
